name: stripe-best-practices
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build and other agents through the skills CLI
short: Stripe's own guide for your agent on choices like Checkout Sessions or PaymentIntents, subscriptions, Connect, tax and key security.
what: The skill gives your agent Stripe's current defaults before it writes integration code: the latest API and SDK versions, which API fits each job, and which deeper reference to read for payments, Connect, billing, tax, Treasury or security. It also carries firm rules, such as never treating webhooks as optional and checking for an active tax registration before turning on automatic tax.
who: Developers building or reviewing a Stripe integration with an AI agent. If you don't use Stripe, you don't need it.
needs: A Stripe account, or the Stripe CLI to create a test sandbox with no sign-up

steps.title: Claude Code
steps.text: Stripe recommends its official plugins, which add agent tools and update automatically. Run this in your project.

steps.title: Cursor
steps.text: Or install through the Cursor marketplace.

steps.title: Any other agent
steps.text: Manually installed skills don't auto-update. Run `npx skills update -y` to get the latest.

steps.title: No Stripe account yet?
steps.text: The skill points to the Stripe CLI (`npm i -g @stripe/cli`) and `stripe sandbox create`, which makes test API keys for you.

try.label: A first prompt
try.text: Ask it to plan one-time payments for your app and explain which Stripe API it chose and why.

watch: The skill steers you to restricted API keys (`rk_`) instead of secret keys (`sk_`).
It tells the agent to build in separate sandboxes, not the shared test mode, for new work.
Stripe also hosts a remote MCP server at mcp.stripe.com that signs in with OAuth.
